title: Macroscopic Stability of a Rapidly Rotating Theta Pinch
abstract: The macroscopic ideal-MHD stability of an axisymmetric mirror device with sonic levels of plasma rotation is analyzed by approximating the plasma equilibrium as a rotating theta pinch possessing an artificial gravity. An eigenmode equation is derived that governs the stability of the equilibrium to small perturbations in the case of an arbitrary plasma angular velocity profile. The stability of the m=1 and m=2 modes is investigated. The plasma is found to be stable to these two modes provided that it is sufficiently short in the axial direction. The critical axial length of the device below which the modes are stabilized first decreases with increasing plasma rotation, attains a minimum value when the rotation is roughly sonic, and then increases with increasing plasma rotation. The value of the plasma rotation off the magnetic axis is found to have a significantly stronger effect on the stability of the modes than the value on the magnetic axis.
